_comment: ADR 0044/0045 — common physics body templates. Per-game entity defs spread these via $extends to get sensible defaults. Override individual fields after the $extends to customize. Bits 1..16 from @lib.physics.layers used here; games with custom layer names can override collision_layer / collision_mask. ADR 0045: `body_type: "character"` creates a CharacterBody3D Node (move_and_slide-driven, the right pick for velocity-controlled actors). Other body_types create raw PhysicsServer3D RIDs.
_sizing_convention: All character_* templates are sized for the NATURAL .glb mesh at state.scale=1.0 (Tripo3D normalizes to bbox.y=1.0). The engine multiplies the body's transform by state.scale at build time (physics_body_builder._apply_state_scale_to_body), so the visible mesh and the capsule scale together uniformly. NEVER author body dimensions sized for the 'final world size' — that double-counts state.scale.

standard_character_player._comment: ADR 0045 — player CharacterBody3D. Sized for a natural humanoid Tripo3D mesh (bbox.y=1.0). Player def's state.scale brings it to final dimensions (e.g. scale=1.7 → 1.7m tall × 0.425m radius human).

standard_character_npc._comment: ADR 0045 — NPC CharacterBody3D. Sized for a natural humanoid Tripo3D mesh (bbox.y=1.0). Same dimensions as player; differs only in collision layer/mask.

standard_character_animal._comment: ADR 0045 — animal CharacterBody3D. Sized for a natural quadruped Tripo3D mesh (bbox.y=1.0). The mesh aspect ratio varies (rabbit is wider than tall, deer is taller than wide), but a capsule sized to bbox.y * scale produces an acceptable approximation. Specific animals scale via state.scale: rabbit=0.35, deer=1.6, wolf=1.0 (unset).

static_decoration_no_collision._comment: For visible-but-non-blocking decoration. No body = no physics overhead. Use this template by NOT declaring a physics block on the entity.

_authoring_note: Templates use $extends syntax: "physics": {"$extends": "@lib.physics.bodies.standard_character_animal"}. State.scale on the entity automatically propagates to the body's transform — author ONE template per archetype, vary instances via state.scale. Custom dimensions per def are an anti-pattern (see .claude/rules/data-demo.md § no escape hatches): if the lib value is wrong for an archetype, fix the lib.
